All 24 read off the evidence you sent - I made no calls of my own, so my side of this is $0. Six settle, eighteen hold. The arithmetic foots both ways: 6 + 18 = 24, and 17 markets carry a charge against your 17 receipts.

SETTLE NO - six, crypto only, Binance 1-minute candles
pm-7203506  ·  BTC between $60,000 and $62,000 on Nov 27  ·  SETTLE NO  ·  closest print the check recorded was 59,958, below the floor, nothing inside the band. $42 of headroom, so it's on the review list below.
pm-5170735  ·  BTC reaches $87,500 in October  ·  SETTLE NO  ·  October high 87,220. Never touched the strike.
pm-5170791  ·  ETH dips to $2,100 in October  ·  SETTLE NO  ·  October low 2,174.08. Floor never tested.
pm-6891215  ·  BTC dips to $62,000 Nov 9–15  ·  SETTLE NO  ·  window low 62,006 - $6 above the strike. That thin margin is on the review list.

pm-6563869  ·  BTC dips to $72,000 Nov 2–8  ·  SETTLE NO  ·  window low 73,510. Clear.

HOLD - eighteen, and the reason is identical on every one

What I'd overrule
No label changes. The six NOs are the connector's outcome and my own read agreeing, and I checked each number against its own question rather than accepting "check_outcome: no" - that's the only reason I can tell you pm-6891215 is a $6 call and pm-7203506 a $42 one. If I'd just taken the outcomes, both would look identical to pm-5170814, which was never in doubt.

One refusal, though. pm-6237004 is the only line in the strip where the paid answer actually produced a verdict - "no" - and I'm holding anyway. An unaudited paid outcome isn't a source. If I let that one through, nothing else in your map means anything.

And one thing I'd change about the evidence itself: $0.29 of the $0.44 went to markets whose rules name no machine-readable source. Under your own rule those answers can't settle anything, so that money bought nothing usable. Same shape as the ghost-purl problem - a free read of the rules first would have caught eleven of them before the call. I'm not second-guessing your connector; I'm saying the gate belongs on "does this market name a checkable source", not on the price of the answer.

Cost
$0.44 across 24 markets, $0.15 of it on the six crypto lines and $0.29 on the eighteen holds. The per-market figures add up to exactly $0.44, and 17 charged lines match 17 receipts. Nothing charged to me - I made no calls, so I'm at $0 for this one.

What a person has to look at
The eighteen holds, first and plainly. Each needs someone holding the market's actual resolution wording plus the authoritative record - match report, certified election result, official announcement. I won't guess at any of them and neither should a summary I write.
Then three crypto lines that depend on wording you didn't send me: pm-6891215 at $6 above the strike and pm-7203506 at $42 below the floor are the fragile ones. Both turn on things I can't see - any print versus close, which day boundary (UTC or ET), which minute counts. A $6 margin on a 1-minute candle read is inside the noise of choosing the window.
pm-7203506 deserves its own note because of its shape rather than its margin: it asks about a band, and one price can't prove a band was never touched. Only a low above the top or a high below the bottom does that. My NO rests on the check's outcome and its value agreeing, not on the value alone, so a person should confirm the connector read the whole of Nov 27.
pm-5170735 is $280 short rather than $42, so it's sturdier - same wording question if the rules say "any print".
Last thing: every window in this batch has already closed, so if any of these are being settled somewhere else too, worth a duplicate check before the same market pays out twice.

Send me the next list whenever you want it read.
